overview: A Hall effect sensor detects the presence and (on linear versions) strength of a nearby magnetic field, with no physical contact needed — just a small magnet passing close by. The simplest digital versions just report 'magnet detected' or not, which makes them a favorite for contactless speed sensing (a magnet glued to a spinning wheel triggers the sensor once per rotation) and for door/lid switches that need to work through a sealed enclosure wall, since magnetic fields pass through most non-metal materials.
simpleSummary: A sensor that notices when a magnet passes close by, with no physical touching needed.

specifications.outputType: Digital (magnet present/absent) on simple modules; analog field-strength on linear Hall sensors
specifications.detectionDistance: A few millimeters to ~1-2cm depending on magnet strength
specifications.responseTime: Very fast, suitable for high-RPM sensing

pinMap.name: OUT
pinMap.function: Digital output — typically LOW when a magnet of the correct polarity is nearby (some modules also expose a raw analog field-strength pin).
pinMap.gotcha: Many Hall sensors only respond to one magnetic pole (north or south) — a magnet flipped the wrong way around won't trigger it at all.

useCases.title: Contactless wheel speed sensing
useCases.scenario: Glue a small magnet to a wheel and count trigger pulses per rotation for speed/distance feedback, with no physical wear like an optical encoder.

useCases.title: Sealed door/lid sensor
useCases.scenario: Detect whether an enclosure's lid is open or closed without a physical switch penetrating the housing.

useCases.title: Brushless motor commutation feedback
useCases.scenario: Some BLDC motors use built-in Hall sensors to report rotor position to the ESC.

oftenConfusedWith: Optical wheel encoder (higher resolution, but wears mechanically/optically over time)
oftenUpgradedTo: Quadrature Hall encoders for direction-aware speed sensing
